candidate.message:
Fix URL validator rejecting a fragment after an empty path (#3016)

* Fix URL validator rejecting a fragment after an empty path

`validate.URL` rejected absolute URLs whose fragment follows an empty
path with no query, such as `https://example.com#frag`. RFC 3986 permits
a fragment after an empty path, and anchor links to a domain root are
common in practice.

Allow `#` to introduce the URL tail so the fragment is accepted. This
also makes a bare `#frag` valid in relative mode, matching the existing
handling of a bare `?query`.

* Add changelog entry for URL fragment fix (:pr:`3016`)

* Remove explanatory comment per review

* credit

---------

Co-authored-by: Steven Loria <git@stevenloria.com>

candidate.subject: Fix nested partial to use attr_name instead of data_key for prefix (#2903)
candidate.message:
Fix nested partial to use attr_name instead of data_key for prefix (#2903)

* Fix nested partial to use attr_name instead of data_key

When building dot-delimited sub_partial for nested schemas, the prefix
was computed from field_name (which is data_key when set) instead of
attr_name. Since users specify partial fields using attribute names like
partial=("nested_field.child",), the prefix needs to match attr_name.

When data_key differs from attr_name, the prefix mismatch caused the
nested partial list to always be empty, so the nested schema never
received the partial option and required fields raised unexpected
validation errors.

* Add test for nested partial with data_key using attr_name prefix

* Update authors and changelog

---------

Co-authored-by: Jared Deckard <jared@shademaps.com>

args.summary: Fixed the nested partial bug (#2903) in src/marshmallow/schema.py's Schema._deserialize method. The prefix used to compute sub_partial fields for nested schema partial loading was incorrectly built from `field_name` (which resolves to the field's `data_key` when set), but partial field-name matching elsewhere (e.g. `attr_name in partial`) uses the field's Python attribute name. Changed `prefix = field_name + "."` to `prefix = attr_name + "."` so the nested partial prefix consistently uses the attribute name. This ensures options() always yields exactly one entry per choice, with missing labels defaulting to "", and no phantom entries when labels outnumber choices (including the empty-choices/extra-labels case). Verified via `tests/test_validate.py::test_oneof_options`, which now passes.

The issue was in the `OneOf.options()` method which used `zip_longest()` to pair choices with labels. This caused extra (choice='', label=remaining_label) pairs when labels outnumbered choices. The fix converts both choices and labels to lists, pads the labels list with empty strings to match the length of choices, then uses regular `zip()` instead of `zip_longest()`. This ensures only as many pairs are created as there are choices, and extra labels are simply ignored.
